site: Land at 28 Godstone Road, Kenley, CR8 5JE

controlledIdentity.proposal: Erection of three terraced dwellings with associated landscaping, cycle/refuse storage and communal garden.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Croydon public application portal via exact application key T6862LJLFL600 and public document index
observed: The exact Croydon application portal URL and application key are publicly corroborated.
Planning Atlas captures twenty-nine linked documents including THE LOCATION PLAN, FLOOD RISK ASSESSMENT, BNG METRIC, final officer report and decision notice.
The Croydon portal rejects direct document retrieval in the current execution environment, so the location/site drawing bytes cannot be admitted into the controlled evidence packet.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Document titles and an index prove that evidence exists; they do not substitute for the source drawing bytes, scale, geometry or measured values.

acquisitionAttempts.route: HM Land Registry title-boundary dataset via Planning Data
observed: Planning Data exposes HM Land Registry title-index polygons as an admissible SCREENING source class.
The exact RP-007 title entity/polygon could not be recovered and identity-bound into this packet from the available interface.
Postcode-centroid geometry is explicitly not substituted for parcel geometry.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Even if recovered, title-index geometry would remain an indicative registered-property extent rather than a determined legal boundary.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Environment Agency LiDAR Composite DTM 1 m
observed: DPL already accepts EA 1 m DTM as SCREENING datum/topography authority when bound to a controlled site extent/frame.
The public corpus and current searches materially corroborate steep/sloping topography but do not provide a controlled ODN terrain sample for RP-007.
Postcode-level elevation around 80 m and narrative descriptions of steep levels are not promoted to R4.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Narrative steepness and postcode elevation are context only; neither is a private topographic survey or a DPL SCREENING datum.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Exact-site planning/refusal context plus Godstone Road/Lower Road public context
observed: Public exact-site material places the parcel between Godstone Road and Lower Road.
Planning-refusal commentary records a proposed vehicle relationship to the A22/Godstone Road and an internal-turning concern.
No controlled frontage/access geometry tied to the application extent has been recovered.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Planning commentary about the applicant scheme does not prove Reference House access geometry or legal access rights.

acquisitionAttempts.route: First-party Croydon weekly decision publication versus captured register/direct public commentary
observed: Croydon's weekly decision publication places 25/03774/FUL beneath a Permission Granted heading for 23 January 2026.
Planning Atlas and later local planning commentary describe refusal on the same date and cite nine refusal grounds.
The conflict is retained and deliberately excluded from candidate-readiness reasoning.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Direct decision-notice bytes would be required before using planning outcome; DPL-15H does not need that outcome to assess R1-R6.

readiness.reason: Exact application identity and UPRN are strong, but no placement-ready application/title geometry has been recovered into the controlled packet.
No controlled boundary shape/dimensions have been recovered that can honestly test the unchanged 12.0 m x 10.8 m Reference House footprint.
A location plan is indexed but its source bytes and controlled geometry were not recovered; postcode/street context is insufficient to author a parcel orientation frame.
Steep topography is well corroborated, but no authoritative terrain sample or usable ODN datum has been bound to the controlled parcel.
The Godstone Road/Lower Road relationship and applicant access concern are known contextually, but exact frontage/access geometry tied to the controlled site extent remains absent.
Application reference, address and UPRN converge on the same real corpus site; the planning-decision label conflict does not make the spatial subject ambiguous.

nextDisposition.reason: RP-007's apparent 29-document advantage does not survive the authority/transport test in the current environment. Repeating more indexed searches would reproduce the same failure class. RP-008 remains the deliberately lower-pathology one-house control and now earns one bounded transport/evidence pass before DPL declares the empirical corpus generally external-evidence-bound.

nextPacket: DPL-15I — RP-008 bounded no-spend spatial-evidence transport test and R1-R6 re-run
